paragraphs: Rav Acha and Ravina were colleagues. Tosafot, Hasho'el et Happarah (I did not find it), write they preceded Rav Pappa. This does not appear correct: Chullin, first chapter, has Ravina and Rav Acha son of Rava before Rav Ashi; Ellu Tereifot likewise places Rav Acha and Ravina before Rav Ashi and Amemar. As above, this is Rav Acha bar Rava. (See Rav Acha bar Rav: there are early Rav Acha and Ravina.) Throughout the Torah Ravina is lenient and Rav Acha stringent; mnemonic chet–chet [ח׳ ח׳, for Acha and chumra, “stringency”], Halikhot Olam. The law follows Ravina, except three where Rabbi Acha is lenient and the law follows him, Chullin 93b; Pesachim 74b; Avodah Zarah 33b and Yevamot 39b require examination. Halikhot Olam 35b says this is when others do not disagree with them. Responsa Chavvot Yair writes, “I did not understand and did not find it.” Jerusalem Talmud, Ma'aser Sheni, chapter 5, halakhah 5: he did not take tithe, so apparently he was a priest (see there). See Rav Acha bar Ravina: he was expressly a priest.
